JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 22-01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, which was driven by his friend by name Nanjegowda, towards Hosakopalu, slowly, on the left side of the Hassan-Belur road, in the middle of H. K.
Hosuru and Kuppalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk.
At that time, the driver of the Alto car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-M-8975, drove the same in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed against the car of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient and underwent surgery.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as LIC Agent and was also doing agriculture and earning Rs.80,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hassan Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the Alto Car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3.
On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Alto car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975 in the alleged accident.
It has further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975 after giving sufficient signal took his vehicle towards eastern side.
But, the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, without taking proper care and caution, came with high speed and collided with the offending car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975.
Both the drivers have contributed equal negligence in causing the said accident.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.

It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as admittedly the accident took place between two vehicles and the petitioner has not arrayed the insured and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05- MP-1619 as party in the present case.
The driver of the petitioner's car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 22- 01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-51-M-8975?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

What order or Award?

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 22-01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, which was driven by his friend by name Nanjegowda, towards Hosakopalu, slowly, on the left side of the Hassan-Belur road, in the middle of H. At that time, the driver of offending Alto car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-M-8975, drove the same in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed against the car of petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as LIC Agent and also doing agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.80,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and whereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.4 & 5 are true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is discharge summary, Ex.P9 are Form No.16A (total 3), Ex.P.10 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.11 is copy of RTC extract, Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 17), Ex.P.13 is authorization letter, Ex.P.14 is copy of MLC extract, Ex.P.15 is case-sheet, Ex.P.16 is clinical notes with disability assessment calculation sheet and Ex.P.17 is X-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Alto car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-M-8975 and dashing the same to on coming car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, in which the petitioner was travelling.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left hand.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.7, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Alto car bearing Reg. No. KA-51-M- 8975.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Alto car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-M- 8975 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said Alto car bearing No.
KA-51-M-8975 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, it has failed to establish the said same.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No. KA-05-MP-1619 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,

There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 22-01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., on Hassan-Belur road, in the middle of H.K. Hosuru & Kuppalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Alto car bearing Reg. No. KA-51-M-8975.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Alto car bearing Reg. No. KA-51-M-8975 and he has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained left distal humerus fracture and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-07-1987.
The accident has taken place on 22-01-2021 at about 5.15 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 35 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left distal humerus fracture and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. open reduction and internal fixation with RECON plate.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 37% to the left arm and 12% to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.3 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.15 case-sheet, Ex.P.16 clinical notes with disability assessment calculation sheet and Ex.P.17 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered left distal humerus fracture and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 22-01-2021 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 18-08-2023, which is after lapse of two years and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fracture is united and the petitioner can do desk job.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as LIC Agent and also doing agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.80,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same he has produced Form No.16A (total 3) and copy of record of rights as per Ex.P.9 and Ex.P11.
From these documents it is clear that, as on the date of accident the petitioner was working as LIC Agent and he was also doing agriculture and was earning handsome income.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that consistently he was earning Rs.80,000/- per month.

The petitioner could have easily proved his monthly or annual income by producing his Income Tax Returns filed for the H.K. Ramesh vs Nayan Kumara on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106986295/
7 recent years, prior to date of accident.
But, the petitioner has not produced the same, for the reasons best known to him.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to hold that, the petitioner has failed to prove his actual income for the purpose of claiming compensation under the head loss of future income and to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,80,000/-.

e) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 35 years is 16.

Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,80,000 X 8/100 X 16 = Rs.2,30,400/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 17 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.1,04,373/- towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has clearly deposed in his evidence that, he has not obtained health insurance policy.
There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said medical bills have already been claimed by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,04,373/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., left distal humerus fracture fracture and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e.
open reduction and internal fixation with RECON plate.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary and Ex.P.15 case-sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 07 days from 22-01-2021 to 28- 01-2021, in Janapriya Hospital, Hassan.
He has also undergone surgery i.e. open reduction and internal fixation with Recon plate.
Further as per P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary and Ex.P.15 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 07 days from 22-01-2021 to 28- 01-2021, in Janapriya Hospital,
Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 = Rs.7,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary and Ex.P.15 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 07 days from 22-01- 2021 to 28-01-2021, in Janapriya Hospital,
Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 7 = Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.

Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Hosakopalu Village, Sravanabelagula Hobli, Channarayapattana Taluk, Hassan District, the accident has taken place on Hassan-Belur road, at the middle of H.K. Hosuru and Kuppalli viillage, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk and he has taken treatment at Janapriya Hospital, Hassan.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:

He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.15,000 x 2 =

viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 35 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,30,400-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,04,373-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6. Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,373/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of H.K. Ramesh vs Nayan Kumara on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106986295/
9 petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Alto car bearing Reg. No. KA-51-M-8975 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,373/-
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,61,373/- (Rupees four lakh sixty one thousand three hundred and seventy three only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident.
The Hassan Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the Alto Car bearing No.KA-51-M-8975 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as admittedly the accident took place between two vehicles and the petitioner has not arrayed the insured and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05- MP-1619 as party in the present case.
The driver of the petitioner's car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in his cross- examination that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619 and there is no negligence on the part of driver of the Alto car bearing Reg. No.
KA-51-M-8975.
13.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 22- 01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-51-M-8975?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or Award?
6.
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 22-01-2021 at about 5.15 p.m., on Hassan-Belur road, in the middle of H.K. Hosuru & Kuppalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Alto car bearing Reg. No. KA-51-M-8975.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MP-1619, it has failed to establish the said same.
4 corroborative evidence produced by the respondent No.2 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05- MP-1619 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Alto car bearing No. KA-51-M-8975.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that,
the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Alto car bearing Reg.
No. KA-51-M-8975.
15.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained left distal humerus fracture and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:

If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
From these documents it is clear that, as on the date of accident the petitioner was working as LIC Agent and he was also doing agriculture and was earning handsome income.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that consistently he was earning Rs.80,000/- per month.
The petitioner could have easily proved his monthly or annual income by producing his Income Tax Returns filed for the H.K. Ramesh vs Nayan Kumara on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106986295/
7 recent years, prior to date of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to hold that, the petitioner has failed to prove his actual income for the purpose of claiming compensation under the head loss of future income and to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2021.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,30,400-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,04,373-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6. Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00
Total Rs. 4,61,373-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,373/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of H.K. Ramesh vs Nayan Kumara on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106986295/
9 petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,373/-
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,61,373/- (Rupees four lakh sixty one thousand three hundred and seventy three only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
